title: Education Training Impact on Farmer Production and Payment
description:

My Approach: Cleaned and analyzed a dataset of 100K farmer records in Excel to compare trained vs untrained farmers across categories (Small, Average, Top 1%). Built clear visualizations for production volume, payment distribution, and average performance.

Key Insights:
1️⃣ Trained farmers demonstrate higher average production and payments across most categories.
2️⃣ The Top 1% show the largest gains, while Small and Average tiers also record measurable improvements.

Impact: The dashboard highlights a clear positive correlation between training attendance and both productivity and income, supporting further investment in farmer education.

Key Insights:
1️⃣ Prices vary by location: Chepareria lags behind (450), while Makutano/Kapenguria lead (~500).
2️⃣ Pest attacks (103) and poor drying facilities (105) are the biggest threats.
3️⃣ Tier 2 & Tier 3 farms dominate production (36K & 60K kg).
4️⃣ Gender price balance is healthy (Male vs Female ~equal).

Business Recommendations:
✅ Target Chepareria farmers with training, inputs, and market linkage to raise their price levels.
✅ Invest in post-harvest handling (drying facilities) and pest management programs.
✅ Channel financing & logistics support to Tier 2 & 3 farms where returns are highest.

Impact: Dashboard insights show where to allocate resources for farmers to maximize incomes and address operational challenges.

title: Tea Production and Bushes Analytics
description:
Problem Statement: Tea estates struggle to optimize production yields across different scales, with surprising efficiency gaps between small and large producers.

Business Objective: Uncover the secrets behind production efficiency variations and identify optimization opportunities across all farm sizes.

My Approach: I developed comprehensive PowerBI dashboards analyzing production metrics across different farm sizes because PowerBI enables deep dive analysis of complex agricultural patterns.

Key Insights:
1️⃣ Small farms (0-500 bushes) achieve extraordinary yields of 127.8 per bush, while larger farms average only 2-3
2️⃣ Large producers (>200k bushes) dominate with 60.5% of total production despite lower per-bush efficiency
3️⃣ Mid-size farms (100k-200k) contribute 39% but struggle with efficiency, caught between scales
4️⃣ Total average yield of 22.51 per bush is heavily skewed by small farm performance
5️⃣ Scale shows inverse relationship with per-bush productivity

Business Recommendations:
✅ Study and replicate small farm management practices
✅ Develop scale-specific optimization strategies
✅ Address mid-size producer challenges
✅ Balance efficiency with production volume
✅ Investigate high-yield techniques for larger operations

Impact: This analysis reveals untapped potential for 40-60% yield improvement by understanding and adapting successful small-scale practices to larger operations.
